_comment: Presentation data for the generated catalog regions (see scripts/sync-catalog.js). Skill existence, names, and counts come from skills/*/SKILL.md — this file only supplies the phase and the editorial one-liners, in the order the README lists them. Adding a skill requires an entry here; sync-catalog.js fails if disk and this file disagree.

skills.name: using-agent-skills
skills.does: Maps incoming work to the right skill workflow and defines shared operating rules
skills.when: Starting a session or deciding which skill applies

skills.name: interview-me
skills.does: One-question-at-a-time interview that extracts what the user actually wants instead of what they think they should want, until ~95% confidence
skills.when: The ask is underspecified, or the user invokes "interview me" / "grill me"
skills.summary: Surface what the user actually wants before any plan, spec, or code exists

skills.name: idea-refine
skills.does: Structured divergent/convergent thinking to turn vague ideas into concrete proposals
skills.when: You have a rough concept that needs exploration
skills.summary: Refine ideas through structured divergent and convergent thinking

skills.name: spec-driven-development
skills.does: Write a PRD covering objectives, commands, structure, code style, testing, and boundaries before any code
skills.when: Starting a new project, feature, or significant change
skills.summary: Requirements and acceptance criteria before code

skills.name: constraint-driven-development
skills.does: Interviews you for a quality bar with sane default thresholds, writes CONSTRAINTS.md, places each check by cost, and catches agents silencing checks or skipping tests to get green
skills.when: No standards are written down, or an agent is producing more than anyone reads
skills.summary: Write the quality bar down once, then enforce it everywhere

skills.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skills.does: Decompose specs into small, verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria and dependency ordering
skills.when: You have a spec and need implementable units
skills.summary: Decompose into small, verifiable tasks

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.does: Thin vertical slices - implement, test, verify, commit. Feature flags, safe defaults, rollback-friendly changes
skills.when: Any change touching more than one file
skills.summary: Thin vertical slices, test each before expanding

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.does: Red-Green-Refactor, test pyramid (80/15/5), test sizes, DAMP over DRY, Beyonce Rule, browser testing
skills.when: Implementing logic, fixing bugs, or changing behavior
skills.summary: Failing test first, then make it pass

skills.name: context-engineering
skills.does: Feed agents the right information at the right time - rules files, context packing, MCP integrations
skills.when: Starting a session, switching tasks, or when output quality drops
skills.summary: Right context at the right time

skills.name: source-driven-development
skills.does: Ground every framework decision in official documentation - verify, cite sources, flag what's unverified
skills.when: You want authoritative, source-cited code for any framework or library
skills.summary: Verify against official docs before implementing

skills.name: doubt-driven-development
skills.does: Adversarial fresh-context review of every non-trivial decision in-flight - CLAIM → EXTRACT → DOUBT → RECONCILE → STOP, with optional user-authorized cross-model escalation
skills.when: Stakes are high (production, security, irreversible), working in unfamiliar code, or a confident output is cheaper to verify now than to debug later
skills.summary: Adversarial fresh-context review of every non-trivial decision

skills.name: frontend-ui-engineering
skills.does: Component architecture, design systems, state management, responsive design, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility
skills.when: Building or modifying user-facing interfaces
skills.summary: Production-quality UI with accessibility

skills.name: api-and-interface-design
skills.does: Contract-first design, Hyrum's Law, One-Version Rule, error semantics, boundary validation
skills.when: Designing APIs, module boundaries, or public interfaces
skills.summary: Stable interfaces with clear contracts

skills.name: browser-testing-with-devtools
skills.does: Chrome DevTools MCP for live runtime data - DOM inspection, console logs, network traces, performance profiling
skills.when: Building or debugging anything that runs in a browser
skills.summary: Chrome DevTools MCP for runtime verification

skills.name: debugging-and-error-recovery
skills.does: Five-step triage: reproduce, localize, reduce, fix, guard. Stop-the-line rule, safe fallbacks
skills.when: Tests fail, builds break, or behavior is unexpected
skills.summary: Reproduce → localize → fix → guard

skills.name: code-review-and-quality
skills.does: Five-axis review, change sizing (~100 lines), severity labels (Nit/Optional/FYI), review speed norms, splitting strategies
skills.when: Before merging any change
skills.summary: Five-axis review with quality gates

skills.name: code-simplification
skills.does: Chesterton's Fence, Rule of 500, reduce complexity while preserving exact behavior
skills.when: Code works but is harder to read or maintain than it should be
skills.summary: Preserve behavior while reducing unnecessary complexity

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.does: OWASP Top 10 prevention, auth patterns, secrets management, dependency auditing, three-tier boundary system
skills.when: Handling user input, auth, data storage, or external integrations
skills.summary: OWASP prevention, input validation, least privilege

skills.name: performance-optimization
skills.does: Measure-first approach - Core Web Vitals targets, profiling workflows, bundle analysis, anti-pattern detection
skills.when: Performance requirements exist or you suspect regressions
skills.summary: Measure first, optimize only what matters

skills.name: git-workflow-and-versioning
skills.does: Trunk-based development, atomic commits, change sizing (~100 lines), the commit-as-save-point pattern
skills.when: Making any code change (always)
skills.summary: Atomic commits, clean history

skills.name: ci-cd-and-automation
skills.does: Shift Left, Faster is Safer, feature flags, quality gate pipelines, failure feedback loops
skills.when: Setting up or modifying build and deploy pipelines
skills.summary: Automated quality gates on every change

skills.name: deprecation-and-migration
skills.does: Code-as-liability mindset, compulsory vs advisory deprecation, migration patterns, zombie code removal
skills.when: Removing old systems, migrating users, or sunsetting features
skills.summary: Remove old systems and migrate users safely

skills.name: documentation-and-adrs
skills.does: Architecture Decision Records, API docs, inline documentation standards - document the *why*
skills.when: Making architectural decisions, changing APIs, or shipping features
skills.summary: Document the why, not just the what

skills.name: observability-and-instrumentation
skills.does: Structured logging, RED metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, symptom-based alerting - instrument as you build
skills.when: Adding telemetry, or shipping anything that runs in production
skills.summary: Structured logs, RED metrics, traces, symptom-based alerts

skills.name: shipping-and-launch
skills.does: Pre-launch checklists, feature flag lifecycle, staged rollouts, rollback procedures, monitoring setup
skills.when: Preparing to deploy to production
skills.summary: Pre-launch checklist, monitoring, rollback plan
